To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the New Zealand White and Californian purebreds are comparable for litter performance, that the New Zealand Whites are the most efficient breed type, that the Californians are the least efficient breed type, and that the Flemish Giant crosses and the Californian X New Zealand White crosses are intermediate for litter performance.

purebred NZW and purebred CAL rabbits are similar in postweaning growth, feed efficiency and survival performance traits; purebred CAL and crossbred FG rabbits have the best postweaning performance traits; purebreds NZW and CAL are less costly to feed than FG crosses; and purebred CAL and FG crossbred rabbits are the best breed types for commercial production of fryers.

the New Zealand White and Californian purebreds had comparable performance traits, and the purebred NZW livers consumed less feed than the crossbreds, and gained weight less rapidly and weighed less than the crossbreads at market age.

there is no difference between NZW, CAL and CXN in any of the traits measured, and that FG crosses are superior to the others in all traits measured except mortality rate.

purebred New Zealand White and Californian litters had similar performances, and the CXN crossbred litter performance was intermediate to that of the CAL and FG crosses.

we have shown the following: 1) The CXN and NZW crosses are the best performing of the four breed types for post-weaning growth and feed efficiency; 2) the FG crosses are better than the CAL purebred and the CXN crosses for post-weaning feed efficiency; 3) the FG crosses and the CXN crossbreds perform comparably for postweaning growth and feed intake.

crossbred rabbits have a better feed to gain conversion ratio than purebred rabbits, and this difference was significant.
crossbred rabbits can outperform purebreds for postweaning traits of interest to the commercial rabbit industry.
